crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: FAIR Data
children.blurb: FAIR Data is a set of guiding principles for research data and metadata: findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable.

children.name: Metadata and Ontologies
children.blurb: Metadata and ontologies in research data and repositories cover the structured descriptions that make data, papers, models, and tools discoverable and the formal vocabularies that give those descriptions shared meaning.

children.name: Federated Sharing of Sensitive Data
children.blurb: Federated sharing of sensitive data covers arrangements where two or more organisations analyse data that cannot be pooled in one place, such as patient records, genomic sequences, financial transactions or personal device data.

children.name: Institutional Knowledge Graphs
children.blurb: Institutional knowledge graphs represent the entities an organization cares about, such as people, projects, publications, datasets, instruments, and administrative units, and the relationships among them.

children.name: Long-Term Digital Preservation
children.blurb: Long-term digital preservation is the work of keeping digital objects usable, understandable, and trustworthy over decades, across changes in hardware, software, formats, and organizations.

sections.body: Research data and repositories is the part of AI work that treats datasets, metadata, models, and provenance as first-class research outputs. AI is used to extract structured claims from papers, align ontologies, detect duplicates, recommend datasets, and monitor repository health. In practice this means pipelines that read a paper, pull out variables, methods, and results, and attach them to persistent identifiers. It also means systems that help researchers find data that matches a question, not just a keyword. The field is less about a single model and more about infrastructure that makes data findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable. The site library holds 288 research papers and 13608 claims extracted from research works, which shows the scale of extraction work.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are solved, including persistent identifiers, basic metadata schemas, and routine deposit workflows. Ontologies exist for many domains, and federated query across institutions is possible when governance and identity are in place. What is not solved is semantic alignment at scale, because different labs use different terms for the same thing and the same term for different things. Sensitive data sharing remains hard because consent, jurisdiction, and re-identification risk do not reduce to a technical protocol. Long-term preservation is also unsolved in practice, because formats change, links rot, and funding for stewardship is uneven. AI can help with metadata generation and anomaly detection, but it cannot guarantee that a repository will remain trustworthy or that an extracted claim is correct.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: FAIR Data sets the baseline expectations for findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reuse. Metadata and Ontologies explains how meaning is captured and aligned so that machines can compare records across sources. Federated Sharing of Sensitive Data covers the governance and privacy techniques that let institutions query data without centralizing it. Institutional Knowledge Graphs connects people, projects, datasets, and claims into a graph that supports discovery and provenance. Long-Term Digital Preservation addresses the harder question of keeping all of this readable and citable over decades. A reader would go to FAIR Data for principles, Metadata and Ontologies for representation, Federated Sharing for controlled access, Institutional Knowledge Graphs for integration, and Long-Term Digital Preservation for stewardship.
